newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end slightly down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end slightly down on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking in Telkom and some medium-sized stocks pushed the Jakarta stock index down on Wednesday despite strong buying interest in some blue-chip stocks, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 0.59 points, or 0.09 percent, to close at 656.07 points after hitting a high of 656.89 points in late afternoon trading. Losers led gainers by 56 to 55, with 55 counters unchanged. Total volume was 212.5 million shares on a turnover of about 409 billion rupiah.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Thursday with as it focuses on counters which have been subject to positive rumours such as possible acquisitions or stock-splits.
"Overall market sentiment was mixed. Buying activity was quite large but it was still lower than net-selling," a local broker said.
He said he did not expected there would be a strong upside trend for the index on Thursday as the many brokers continued to adopt a one-day trading attitude, cashing in gains at the end of the day.

Blue-chips including car maker Astra International, Indosat and Sampoerna and banking stocks such as Bank Negara Indonesia and Bank International Indonesia were among the targets of foreign buyers, brokers said.

Astra International local shares rose 250 rupiah to 5,950 rupiah on 897,500 shares on fresh buying. Brokers said it was boosted by its sharp increase in the company's foreign-owned stock, traded separately, which also rose 250 rupiah to 7,300 rupiah on 478,000 shares.
"The launch of the new family-car Kijang has boosted sentiment with the expectation it will reinforce its position as the leader in the car market," a broker with London-based securities said.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 250 rupiah to 13,250 rupiah on 355,500 shares on fresh buying due to its fundamentals, brokers said.
Telkom, the Jakarta bourse's heaviest stock, fell 100 rupiah to 4,100 rupiah on 4.6 million shares which in line with its lower ADS which closed at 34-1/2 in New York.
Asia Equity in its January journal said: "Sampoerna still offers upside of 12 percent based on the current share price of 13,375 rupiah and a target of 15,000 rupiah."

"The current price-earnings growth ratio of 0.9 times is attractive compared to Gudang Garam's 1.3 times. And we expect to see Sampoerna outperform the market over the rest of this year," the report said.
Satellite and international telephone operator Indosat rose 175 rupiah to 6,825 rupiah on 1.1 million shares, boosted by its higher ADS price in New York overnight of 28-3/8.
Bank Negara Indonesia rose 25 rupiah to 1,300 rupiah on 34.3 million shares, while Bank International Indonesia rose 25 rupiah to 1,750 on 2.8 million shares.
Property firm Summarecon, heavyweight Telkom and drug maker Kalbe Farma were among the losers on profit-taking, brokers said.
Summarecon fell 150 rupiah to 1,250 rupiah on 18.6 million shares after rising sharply in the last two day on talk of acquisitions which has been denied by a company official.
Property and hotel firm Jakarta International rose 150 rupiah to 2,200 rupiah on 8.2 million shares following news that it was planning to make a bonds issue worth 500 billion rupiah, brokers said.
